Q: return the updated value after running the update query in mysql A:

No, you can't. And I don't see, why you worry about it. I'd guess, that rid is your primary key. The SELECT afterwards should therefore be so fast, that you'll hardly notice it.

Q: How to reach at the next row A:

Use limit <offset>, <number of records to fetch>

To get only the 3rd record use

select * from your_table
order by qid
limit 2, 1

to get all records starting from the 3rd one use

select * from your_table
order by qid
limit 2, 999999999

Q: Explicit control of initialization & destruction of global variables A:

Generally speaking, destruction of statics happens in reverse of their order of construction (which is unspecified if the globals are defined in different translation units)

If you explicitly require control over order of construction and/or destruction of objects, statics are a very poor choice.

One option may be to have a single object that contains pointers to the other (types of) objects you need. Then you will have explicit control over lifetime of the contained/managed objects (e.g. constructor of the static instantiates the set of objects, destructor destroys in a desired order, other member functions - if needed - selectively destroy the managed objects [and track what it does - for example by nulling pointers - to avoid a destroying an object a second time in the destructor]).

That single object can be a static, but you will still have the same problem with order of construction and destruction relative to any other statics.

Q: selenium.common.exceptions.WebDriverException: Message: Service chromedriver unexpectedly exited. Status code was: 1 A:

The problem is that you're missing ChromeDriver,

First, find which version of Chrome are you using:

  • Click on the three dots on the top right corner (in Chrome)
  • Help
  • About Google Chrome

Second, find and download the right version of ChromeDriver

  • https://chromedriver.chromium.org/downloads

Third, Unzip the package and move it to the usr/local/bin folder.

(usr/local/bin path worked for me on macOS, might be different for different OS)

Q: Laravel eloquent query builder - Sum with group on relationship A:

In the generated SQL, you need to select the column you group by, and you need to call the get() after the groupBy or else you'd be calling the groupBy on the collection, not the query builder object. So you should be able to do:

Transaction::selectRaw('transactionType.category, sum(amount) as amount')
->with('transactionType')
->groupBy('transactionType.category')
->get();

Or Less Eloquent

DB::table('transaction')
->join(
    'transaction_type',
    'transaction_type.id',
    '=',
    'transaction.transaction_type_id'
)->selectRaw('transationType.category, sum(amount)')
->groupBy('transactionTyle.category')
->get();
